translationRepairs: The following year, after Li Cun'an recovered Zhen Prefecture, he sent Guo Chongtao to inspect its treasury. Many offered him precious gifts, but he accepted nothing and bought only books.
The following year, after Li Cunshen recovered Zhen Prefecture, he sent Guo Chongtao to inspect its treasury. Many offered him precious gifts, but he accepted nothing and bought only books.
Focus unit names 李存審; 審 is shěn, so Li Cun'an is a false romanization. Li Cunshen matches the Chinese and leaves the rest of the idiomatic sentence intact.
The next year, Li Cun'an recovered Zhenzhou and dispatched Chongtao to inspect its treasury stores. Some tried to bribe him with precious goods; he took not one thing, but only purchased books.
The next year, Li Cunshen recovered Zhenzhou and dispatched Chongtao to inspect its treasury stores. Some tried to bribe him with precious goods; he took not one thing, but only purchased books.
Same focus Chinese 李存審 requires Li Cunshen in the literal field; Cun'an misreads 審 and the proposed replacement is otherwise unchanged and accurate.
Emperor Mingzong was at Yan, and all lines of communication had been severed.
Emperor Mingzong was at Yun, and all lines of communication had been severed.
Focus unit has 明宗在鄆; 鄆 is yùn (Yun), not 燕/Yan. Replacing Yan with Yun corrects the place without altering the rest.
Mingzong was at Yan; messages and post stations were cut off.
Mingzong was at Yun; messages and post stations were cut off.
Literal likewise misrenders 鄆 as Yan; Yun is the correct romanization for the same Chinese phrase.
Guo Chongtao addressed him, saying, "Duan Ning has cut the river crossings. If our army does not advance south, how can Yan be held?
Guo Chongtao addressed him, saying, "Duan Ning has cut the river crossings. If our army does not advance south, how can Yun be held?
Speech closes with 鄆州安能保守; 鄆州 is Yun Prefecture, so idiomatic Yan is wrong. Yun preserves the sentence's brevity and meaning.
Chongtao submitted, saying: "Duan Ning has blocked and cut off the ford routes. If the imperial army does not go south, how can Yan Prefecture be kept and defended!
Chongtao submitted, saying: "Duan Ning has blocked and cut off the ford routes. If the imperial army does not go south, how can Yun Prefecture be kept and defended!
Literal Yan Prefecture contradicts 鄆州; Yun Prefecture is the accurate rendering of the same clause.
Chief Palace Attendant Li Shaohong proposed abandoning Yan, concluding a treaty with Liang with the Yellow River as the border and a mutual pledge against raiding.
Chief Palace Attendant Li Shaohong proposed abandoning Yun, concluding a treaty with Liang with the Yellow River as the border and a mutual pledge against raiding.
Focus unit 請棄鄆州 refers to abandoning Yun Prefecture; idiomatic Yan is a place-name error, and Yun is the correct fix.
Chief Palace Attendant Li Shaohong petitioned to abandon Yan Prefecture, ally with the men of Bian with the river as boundary, and have no mutual invasion or raid.
Chief Palace Attendant Li Shaohong petitioned to abandon Yun Prefecture, ally with the men of Bian with the river as boundary, and have no mutual invasion or raid.
Literal Yan Prefecture likewise misreads 鄆州; Yun Prefecture matches the Chinese.
I have learned that the Liang have diverted the river from Hua to Yan, so crossing south requires boats.
I have learned that the Liang have diverted the river from Hua to Yun, so crossing south requires boats.
Unit has 自滑至鄆; the endpoint is Yun, not Yan. The proposed idiomatic change corrects only that place name.
I hear the men of Bian have breached the river from Hua to Yan; without boats and oars one cannot cross.
I hear the men of Bian have breached the river from Hua to Yun; without boats and oars one cannot cross.
Literal Hua to Yan misreads the same 至鄆; Yun is required by the Chinese.

Their best troops are massed under Duan Ning, while Wang Yanzhang harasses Yan daily. They mean to pin us with a great army on our southern frontier while trusting the breached river to keep us from crossing south and reconquering Wenyang. That is the Liang plan.

Their best troops are massed under Duan Ning, while Wang Yanzhang harasses Yun daily. They mean to pin us with a great army on our southern frontier while trusting the breached river to keep us from crossing south and reconquering Wenyang. That is the Liang plan.
Clause 王彥章日寇鄆境 means raids on the Yun border; idiomatic Yan is wrong, and Yun is accurate.

I also hear that elite troops are all under Duan Ning's command; Wang Yanzhang daily raids the Yan border. They both with a great army press our southern frontier and rely on the breached river, thinking we cannot cross south—their aim is to recover Wenyang. This is the Bian people's stratagem.

I also hear that elite troops are all under Duan Ning's command; Wang Yanzhang daily raids the Yun border. They both with a great army press our southern frontier and rely on the breached river, thinking we cannot cross south—their aim is to recover Wenyang. This is the Bian people's stratagem.
Literal Yan border likewise contradicts 鄆境; Yun border is the correct place reading.
He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanziao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to summon the puppet Fengzhou military commissioner Wang Chengjie.
He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanxiao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to summon the puppet Fengzhou military commissioner Wang Chengjie.
Focus unit names 康延孝; 延孝 is Yanxiao, so Yanziao is a misspelling. Kang Yanxiao restores the standard romanization without other changes.
He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanziao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to persuade the pseudo-Fengzhou Military Commissioner Wang Chengjie.
He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanxiao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to persuade the pseudo-Fengzhou Military Commissioner Wang Chengjie.
Literal has the same misspelled Kang Yanziao for 康延孝; Kang Yanxiao is the correct personal-name romanization.
